reasons: The cited Section 4(a) does confer a Customer convenience right: the preamble defines The Associated Press as "Customer" and each of Customer and Kubient as a "Party", so "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" gives us a for-any-reason exit; the failed deterministic regex is explainable as a defined-term phrasing variant, not a substantive gap.

Notice period of 90 days sits inside the fallback's 60–90 day window, and the term is a 1-year Initial Term with 1-year auto-renewals, so the detection trigger for 'no Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months' is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in.

Vendor's mirror right is on the same 90 days' notice, so it does not fall into walk-away territory (which requires Vendor convenience on fewer than 90 days); Kubient's entitlement to fees 'generated during the termination period' is bounded by the ~90-day notice window rather than being an uncapped early-termination penalty, consistent with the fallback's 3-month fee cap.

Correctly treated as compliant-at-fallback with no redline and no counterparty comment; the shortfalls versus preferred (90 rather than 30 days, Vendor's right not confined to term-end, no pro-rata refund in a revenue-share model where Customer does not prepay) are properly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, per the minor sub-element rule.
